cases.name: S1 naive swap loses the detached operation's effect (control, reproduces the known failure)
S2 a globally gated swap preserves the detached operation's effect
S3 a per-target gate on envA does not protect envB's in-flight work on the same host
S4 a global gate protects every target the host owns
S5 a new operation for the gated scope is refused while the window is held, and admitted again once released
S6 a real V1->V2 respawn preserves V1's operation, serves a new one on a different PID, and refuses every concurrent admission attempt during the handover
